women.$comment: No women's sport anywhere (Parth, 29 Sep 2026: a Women's Champions League match showed as 'AS Roma v FC Barcelona' with nothing saying it was the women's game). The title often doesn't say so: Polymarket puts it in a tag, the series and the description, Kalshi in the market's address (KXWTA...). So a sport market is dropped when its title, tags, address or description match 'pattern'.

world_us.$comment: US markets that move the whole world are kept, whatever the exclusions below say (Parth, 28 Sep 2026: 'U.S. politics that impacts the world should be added'). Each pattern is matched on the title. Kept: who wins the US presidential election (not primaries, nominees, states or parties), Federal Reserve rate decisions, US tariffs, and US oil and fuel exports. Still out: Congress, governors, mayors, approval ratings, what Trump says or does, fundraising, Fed chair picks.
patterns: ^(?!.*(nominee|primary|primaries|\bparty\b|parties|district|electoral vote|popular vote|margin|turnout|swing state|win .{0,20}\bstates?\b)).*(presidential election winner|win the (20\d\d )?(us |u\.s\. )?presidential election|(us|u\.s\.) presidential election|presidential election 20\d\d|20\d\d presidential election)

us_politics.$comment: Polymarket markets tagged with any of 'tags' are US domestic politics and stay off, unless they also carry one of 'unless' (world affairs, foreign elections; 'culture' and 'science' keep curiosities like aliens). Added 28 Sep 2026 after an ActBlue market got through (Parth: 'keep away').

exclude.$comment: Parth's standing exclusions: US domestic politics, US economic policy including the Fed, American football, baseball, hockey and college sport, esports, crypto price ladders, weather, post and view counts. NBA, film, TV and celebrities are in (26 Sep 2026). Crypto out entirely (26 Sep 2026).

follow_rule: A single match (A vs B) never makes a card. It shows under its sport's Coming up when it starts within a week and involves someone followed (any trade from fixture_min_volume_followed) or a name in that topic's notable list (min_volume_24h).

areas.label: Miscellaneous
areas.note: Trending anyway: the busiest markets that fit nowhere above.

$comment_pm_tags: topics[].pm_tags: Polymarket tag slugs read for that subject on top of the busiest 400 overall. topics[].notable: teams and players whose matches count as famous enough for Coming up.
$comment_rank: Each subject: must-haves first (topics[].must, regex on title and outcomes; shown on as little as must_min_volume a day), then follows, then topics[].prefer, then the rest by score (0.6 x today's trade + 0.4 x lifetime trade / 30). 3 to 9 per subject: all must-haves and follows, at least per_topic_min, more only while score >= extra_min_score and extra_min_share of the subject's best.

board.$comment: The tide board, seven slots in order: best AI model, Real Madrid, football, Formula 1, cricket, world, most traded. Labels name the market; the gauge shows its leader; the followed side's chance rides on a chip. Each slot falls back to its subject's top market.

follow_note: Barcelona is followed as a rival (a hatewatch), not a team Parth supports.

why._about: One-line notes under markets, written by Gemini from news that Andaaza finds with Tavily (or, if Tavily fails, NewsData.io when NEWSDATA_API_KEY is set). Two kinds: 'why it moved' (a big move) and 'why it leads' (a steady favourite). Optional by design: with no GEMINI_API_KEY or TAVILY_API_KEY, or if either service fails or runs out, cards show only their usual lines and nothing else changes. Currents never get a note.
why.points_rule: Why it moved: the favourite moved at least this many points in a day, a week or thirty days (shortest window first), on a spread of at most max_spread points, in real money. Anywhere on the page except Currents. Week and month changes come from Polymarket only.
why.moved_rule: One note per move. It stays while the move stays above keep_share of the threshold, and is rewritten only when the price moves regrow_points more, the move turns round, or the favourite changes. When the news explains nothing, it is not asked again until the price moves miss_regrow more.
why.leads_rule: Why it leads: the favourite is at least min percent now and was at least min a week ago (a day ago on Kalshi), with no big move, up to max (settled questions are not shown at all). On the tide board, the first three cards of each subject, and any must-have (★) wherever it is; not other rows, Miscellaneous or Where the money is. Rewritten when the facts behind it change: after the leader's next match (after_match_hours after its start, if it is listed in Coming up), when the price has moved regrow_points either way since the note was written, when the favourite changes, and at the latest every refresh_days days.
why.matches_rule: Why X is favoured, for a single match: the tide board's match gauges and the Coming up matches of anyone followed (set which to "all" for every Coming up match, about 4 more searches a day). Written once, within hours_before hours of the start, from the last news_days days of news; rewritten only if the favourite changes.
why.short_lived: Weekly charts and dated rankings ('Billboard Hot 100 (Oct 10, 2026)', 'this week') get no notes: they reset too often.
why.budget_rule: Each note costs one Tavily search (1,000 free a month) and one Gemini call (free key: 20 a day on each Flash model, 500 on Flash-Lite). At most per_reading notes a reading and per_month a month. A day (IST) may use what is left of the month spread over the days left, at least per_day and at most per_day_max, so a quiet start never strands the month's allowance (Parth, 28 Sep 2026: 'only 1 note is super bad'). A failed note gets one second Gemini try on the same news, told what failed (no extra search). A service error pauses notes for pause_minutes, and not at all when another note in the same reading worked; a used-up allowance pauses six hours. Order: in this order: the tide board (moves, then leaders and matches), favourites (followed matches, must-haves, follows), other moves, other leaders. A reading happens at most every fifteen minutes however many people visit, so more visitors never means more notes. Both keys are free plans with no card: if a limit is ever reached the service refuses, notes pause and nothing is charged.
why.query_rule: The news search is the question without dates, years or brackets (league codes spelt out by query_names), led by the favourite's name and, for a move, the rival that moved most the other way (5 points or more); for a lead, the runner-up.
why.models_rule: Tried in order. On the free key the Flash models allow 20 calls a day each and Flash-Lite 500 (AI Studio → Rate limits); a model whose day is used up is skipped until midnight Pacific (12:30 pm IST), one that is busy or retired hands over to the next. To change model, edit this list.

sources.$comment: Where a note may come from (Parth, 28 Sep 2026: Antonelli '242 points' came from an Instagram post when he had 302; an Arsenal 'title' from Facebook; a Ballon d'Or overtake from X). Only dated news sites: social sites in 'blocked' are never searched or used, and an undated item is skipped. Every number in a note must appear in the item it came from. A note with a number must come from news at most numbers_days old, and a saved one with a number is rewritten after numbers_days (standings, points and totals change every weekend).

voice: You write one short note for Andaaza, a public page that shows what prediction markets expect. Readers anywhere in the world may know nothing about the subject.

Use only the numbered news you are given. Give as pick the number of the item that best supports your note. If none of them explains it, give pick 0 and an empty note. Never guess or fill in from memory.

The note gives the cause: what happened, or the standing fact that explains it, with names, numbers and dates from the news. Name the favourite or the rival it is about. Present or past tense, whichever reads naturally. It may say what the event means for the question.

Aim for about 120 characters; never more than 140. One sentence. Write every number as digits (7 wins from 7 matches, +24 goal difference, $50 billion, 3rd). Do not repeat the percentages or the move (the page shows them) and do not mention bettors, traders, odds or the market.
Plain and exact, in the spirit of a good newspaper editor: no hedging (reportedly, likely, may, appears), no hype adjectives, no em dashes, no questions or exclamation marks.
why.checks_rule: A note is thrown away (never edited) when it is longer than max_chars, has an em dash, a question or exclamation mark, a banned word, ends in a comma and one of banned_tails (', highlighting the growing importance of'), or does not name any of the market's contenders.

decided.rule: A question counts as decided, and gives way (a race winner hands the F1 slot to the next race), when its leader is above 98.5%, or at least share percent once the question is past the date it was due to be settled. Kalshi keeps finished races open a week for the official result; this stops a finished race sitting on the board. A question still ahead of its date stays, however sure.

added.$comment: When a market was first shown on Andaaza. A card shows "Added 5 h ago" and, for the first new_hours, a small "New" label; hovering shows when its exchange listed it. A card is recognised by all its exchange addresses (so a change of the leading exchange never makes it new). The record began on 28 Sep 2026: for its first warm_days only markets listed after that can be dated (older ones may have been here before; they show nothing). A market that leaves the page is remembered for remember_days, so rotating in and out never makes it new again.

marks.$comment: Logos, flags and faces beside names come from the shared library (github.com/thefirstparth/marks), copied by `npm run marks`. faces: false shows no photos of people at all; each person shows the flag they play under instead (Parth, 28 Sep 2026: "remove all human faces for now; only flags and logos"). Set true and run `npm run marks` to bring faces back.
